facts.text: Saint Stephens Church was first authorized by the House of Burgesses in 1710 and served as the parish's primary worship site until after the Revolution.
The upper church of Saint Stephens housed the earliest known colonial Virginia sundial, donated by Colonel James Taylor, great‑grandfather of Presidents Zachary Taylor and James Madison.
In 1972 the site was listed on the Virginia Landmarks Register, and a year later added to the National Register of Historic Places.
The lower church, rebuilt between 1730 and 1734, showcases Flemish bond brickwork and a cruciform plan typical of colonial Anglican architecture.
Saint Stephens Church sits beside the Mattaponi River in central King and Queen County, a location that shaped early colonial settlement patterns.
The parish originated from a 1683 petition by local inhabitants in what was then part of New Kent County, reflecting early Tidewater settlement.
